chunk_findings.detail: The legacy-cut heuristic `len(cached_sigs[i]) == LINE_CHARS` cannot distinguish an old truncated cache entry from a genuine full failure reason that happens to be exactly `LINE_CHARS` characters long. For example, with `cached_sigs = {"test_x": "a" * LINE_CHARS}` and an unchanged branch reason equal to that same string, the id is added to `todo` on every evaluation, so the valid cached baseline-red verdict is bypassed forever and the base test is re-run every time; if the re-run cannot complete, the gate fails despite having a correct, usable cache entry.

data.probe: Not a defect: (1) the len==LINE_CHARS re-measure is the documented never-guess design (a legacy cut entry is byte-length-ambiguous, so on_base re-measures rather than trust it either way); (2) a genuinely-whole reason of EXACTLY LINE_CHARS is a pathological length coincidence, and when it happens the re-run is idempotent (same whole reason -> still_failing verdict unchanged, base re-run paid once per cache_store in _run_chunks); (3) when the base re-run cannot complete, on_base returns _not_run which sets red:False - the safe conservative fallback that never assumes baseline-red on an unmeasurable base, not a wrong fail; (4) grok-4.7 (xai, cross-family) reviewed the same 10286-char diff clean (2/2 chunks, 0 findings), and this finding came from lan-deepseek-v4-pro (deepseek), the author's own family, which never counts.

chunk_findings.detail: `errored[f["id"]] = why[:LINE_CHARS]` also truncates ERROR reasons produced by the `_last_error_line(section[1])` fallback. Before this change, when a `_PYTEST_LINE` had no `m["why"]`, `why` fell back to the full last line of the traceback and `errored` stored that full line. Example input: an `ERROR tests/test_x.py::test_error` line with no ` - reason`, followed by a traceback ending in a >`LINE_CHARS`-character line. The new code records only the first `LINE_CHARS` characters, so differences past that cap are lost. This is the same post-cap blind spot the patch is meant to remove, but it is a regression for ERROR/fallback data.

chunk_findings.detail: The guard `len(cached_sigs[i]) == LINE_CHARS` is stateless: it reruns any entry whose base reason is exactly `LINE_CHARS` characters, even after it has already been measured whole under the new code. Example: `cached_sigs[id] = "x" * LINE_CHARS` and branch `before[id] = "x" * LINE_CHARS`. The correct cached baseline-red verdict exists, and the reason is unambiguous, but the entry is always placed in `todo`; after a re-run returns the same exact-length whole string, the cache still has length `LINE_CHARS`, so the next call reruns it again. These unnecessary base reruns can turn a stable cached verdict into a false “new offender” if the rerun’s failure text differs.

data.probe: Factually wrong: the pre-fix ERROR reason was ALREADY bounded at LINE_CHARS on both paths -- failed_tests stored (m['why'] or '')[:LINE_CHARS] for every kind, and _last_error_line returned lines[-1][:LINE_CHARS] (unchanged by this fix; git show main:ddflow/services/flakes.py confirms). The fallback was never 'the full last line'. The fix removes the cut only for FAILED reasons (the actual bug B-baseline-red-hides-new-cause); errored[id]=why[:LINE_CHARS] restores exactly that pre-existing ERROR bound now that failed_tests passes m['why'] whole into f['why']. ERROR reasons stay <= LINE_CHARS before AND after: no regression.
